subject: Renewal pricing — capacity hard cap & overage guard proposal
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.infer>
To: Claire Wu <claire.wu@veloxware.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.infer>, priyom_das@redwood.infer
Date: Sat, 25 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing — capacity hard cap & overage guard proposal

Hi Claire,

Thanks again for carving out time last week. Based on Veloxware's growth signals and the usage snapshot we saw in Q1, I wanted to put a compact proposal on the table that addresses two customer asks we heard: predictability for unit cost during spikes, and a simple path to uplift committed capacity.

Proposal (high level):
- 12-month renewal with a 9-month price hard cap on per-token rate (cap applies to base committed units only).
- Overage guard: any usage above commit up to 20% will be billed at a capped overage rate (lower than standard list), and excess beyond 20% billed at normal overage rates.
- Conversion of outstanding credits: Veloxware's remaining Q2 credits (as discussed) convert to one-time burst tokens usable during spikes.
- Qualification: a modest 10% commit uplift in months 1–3 to lock the price cap and overage guard.

Attachments: Veloxware_Usage_Summary_Q1-2028.csv (usage by product, p95 latency), Amendment_draft_v3.docx (commercial language).

Would you be open to a quick 30-min sync tomorrow to walk numbers and confirm if the 9-month cap or a 12-month cap is preferred? If procurement wants a longer hard cap term, we can show a tiered tradeoff in the amendment.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.infer | +1 415-555-0143

---

From: Claire Wu <claire.wu@veloxware.com>

Cc: Veloxware SalesOps <salesops@veloxware.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing — capacity hard cap & overage guard proposal

Marcus — thanks for the clear write-up and for sending the usage snapshot. A few quick notes from our side after an initial skim: 

- We appreciate the overage guard idea; predictability for the next 12 months is a priority for finance. Would Redwood consider a 12-month hard cap rather than 9?
- On commit uplift: procurement will want to see conservative numbers. Can you show an alternative where the price cap is preserved with no uplift but a slightly higher cap premium?
- We have an internal spike in June (product launch) so the burst token conversion is helpful — want to make sure those tokens are usable across both inference and embedding requests.

I attached our internal usage export (velox_usage_q1.csv) to show per-service breakdown. I can get procurement and cloud finance on a short call if you and Lauren can make time next week.

Claire Wu
Head of Cloud Platform | Veloxware
claire.wu@veloxware.com

Claire — really helpful context, thanks. Quick thoughts: 

- Option A (no uplift): 12-month hard cap available at a ~6% higher cap premium versus the 9-month with uplift. This avoids asking procurement for additional committed spend upfront.
- Option B (light uplift): the original proposal (10% uplift first quarter) keeps the cap premium ~3% and gives you better overage economics (lower overage rate to 20%).

We can make the burst tokens apply to both generation and embedding pipelines — we'll reflect that in the amendment.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll draft a comparison table and put both options with projected unit economics (attach to amendment).
2) If procurement wants firm commitment language, loop in legal (I've CC'd Priyom for redline support).
3) We run a single procurement call next Tue or Wed — I'll coordinate with Lauren to find times.

If that works I'll start drafting the side-by-side and send a redline for procurement to review.

Marcus
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Claire — looping in billing/procurement notes so expectations are clear from our side.

Billing/legal notes: 
- If Veloxware selects Option A (no uplift, 12-month cap with higher premium), we can accept that commercially but will require the renewal amendment to state explicit tranche definitions for burst token usage and a PO referencing the amendment.
- If Option B (uplift) is chosen, we can apply the lower overage rates immediately upon amendment signature; we will commit those lower rates for the 12-month renewal period.
- Our legal team prefers DocuSign for execution; I will prepare a redline and a final DocuSign packet once commercial language is confirmed.

I attached Amendment_redline_v1.docx with our initial commercial/legal framing. Priyom — could you review for any clause we should avoid (data residency change requests, audit scope)?

Marcus / Lauren — thanks for the quick turnaround and the options. Procurement took a look this afternoon and the preference is Option A (12-month hard cap with slightly higher premium) to avoid committing additional spend right before our June launch. Procurement asked for two final clarifications before we sign: 

1) Please confirm burst token applicability to embeddings + generation (looks good per your note).
2) We need the overage guard threshold and rate spelled out in the amendment (i.e., 0–20% at capped overage rate X, >20% at standard overage rate Y).

If you can reflect those in the redline, we can push this through procurement and e-sign. We'll route PO creation to SalesOps and finish internal approvals today.

Claire
